validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed independently. This segment is the real, named project '桂东南环网梧州—岑溪段天然气管道项目（龙圩段）' (Guidongnan/Southeast-Guangxi Ring Network, Wuzhou-Cenxi section, Longwei sub-segment) — GEM's segment name 'Wuzhou-Cexi' is an abbreviation of Wuzhou-Cenxi (Cexi = typo for Cenxi/岑溪). Confirmed via TWO genuinely independent origins: (1) Guangxi provincial government administrative records — Guangxi Development & Reform Commission project approval (fgw.gxzf.gov.cn, dated 2022-04-14 per search snippet) and Guangxi Natural Resources Dept land-use approvals for both the Longwei section (dnr.gxzf.gov.cn, 2024-04-01) and the Cenxi section (dnr.gxzf.gov.cn), plus a Wuzhou municipal government state-land-allocation approval (2024-07-26, mirrored at faxin.cn) — all describing the same named project and route; (2) a construction-progress news story datelined 2024-11-18 ("转自：梧州发布" — sourced from the official Wuzhou municipal government media channel, syndicated by both news.qq.com and finance.sina.com.cn) reporting the project 90% complete with expected full completion end of Dec 2024. NOTE: the two news outlets are NOT counted as independent of each other (both explicitly credit '梧州发布' as the original source) — only the government-approval-document track and the news-wire track are treated as the two independent origins. IMPORTANT LIMITATION: the *.gxzf.gov.cn government domains (fgw.gxzf.gov.cn, dnr.gxzf.gov.cn) are unreachable from this research environment (persistent ConnectTimeout on repeated retries via url_verifier.py and WebFetch/curl, same IP 202.103.252.132 for both hosts) — this is a network-level block, not a sign the documents don't exist; their content was confirmed via search-engine indexing/snippets quoting the approval text verbatim (matching Longwei/Cenxi place names, land areas, dates), but I could not get a url_verifier PASS on them, so they are NOT included in proposed_refs. Only the news.qq.com URL cleared url_verifier and is cited below. SPEC: news source gives total line length 59km (Cenxi portion 29.5km) vs GEM LengthKnown=60.00km — a ~1.7% discrepancy, most likely design-vs-as-built rounding, not material. Capacity: news gives 5.9亿立方米/年 = 0.59 bcm/y — an EXACT match to GEM's Capacity=0.59/CapacityUnits=bcm/y. Start point 'Wuzhou compressor station, Dapo Town [大坡镇], Longwei District' and end point 'Cenxi distribution station, Daye Town, Cenxi City' both match GEM's StartLocation/EndLocation. Diameter (406.40mm) and Pressure (6.30 MPa) could not be independently corroborated (no source found with pipe-spec detail) — left as-is, unconfirmed but plausible for this capacity class. CLASSIFICATION: correctly a gas transmission pipeline; correctly grouped under the regional 'Guangxi Gas Pipeline Network' entity alongside its many other segments — not a gathering/process line. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 43-row roster — no other row references Wuzhou, Cenxi, or Longwei District; this is not a relabel of any other segment in scope. ATTRIBUTION: Operator/Owner recorded as '国家管网集团西南管道有限责任公司南宁输油气分公司' (PipeChina Southwest Pipeline Co., Nanning Oil & Gas Transport Branch) — plausible as the PipeChina regional branch covering Guangxi gas assets, but I could not find a source naming this specific company in connection with the Wuzhou-Cenxi/Longwei segment specifically; left unresolved (see fills), not flagged as wrong. FuelSource='Sino-Myanmar Gas Pipeline' is also unresolved: Wuzhou/Cenxi sit at the SE edge of Guangxi near the Guangdong border, geographically on the opposite side of the province from the Sino-Myanmar pipeline's Yunnan entry point; the corridor is at least as plausible to be fed from West-East Gas Pipeline Line 2's Guangzhou-Nanning extension (cited elsewhere on this same wiki page) as from Sino-Myanmar gas routed across the whole province. Genuinely could not confirm either way — flagged as an open question, not a confident error.

fills.researcher_notes: Source explicitly describes this as a 天然气管道 (natural gas pipeline) project; confirms Fuel=Gas.

Could not find any source connecting the Wuzhou-Cenxi/Longwei segment specifically to the Sino-Myanmar Gas Pipeline as its upstream feed. Geographically this SE-Guangxi corridor is at least as plausible to draw from the West-East Gas Pipeline Line 2 Guangzhou-Nanning extension (also cited on this wiki page for a different segment). Left unfilled rather than fabricate a ref; flagged in validity as an open attribution question.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Newest dated evidence found is 2024-11-18 (Wuzhou municipal government media release, syndicated by news.qq.com and finance.sina.com.cn): project 90% complete, workers doing process/electrical/instrumentation installation and commissioning, full completion expected end of Dec 2024. That is well within normal construction timelines and does not trigger the >=2y dormancy rule (which applies to 'proposed' status, not active construction with recent progress evidence). Searched extensively (Chinese-language queries across multiple phrasings: 竣工/投产/通气/全线贯通, 2025) for any later confirmation that the pipeline actually entered service after the targeted Dec-2024 completion, and for local government portals (Wuzhou, Cenxi city sites) — found none. So while it is quite likely operating by now (per the Nov-2024 90%-complete/Dec-2024-target evidence), I cannot independently confirm a transition to 'operating' status, and recommend 'construction' stand for this pass with a flag to recheck for an operating/commissioning date on the next sweep.

summary: P4731 (Guidongnan Ring Network Wuzhou-Cenxi/Longwei gas segment) is a real, independently-confirmed project (Guangxi DRC approval + Natural Resources land-use approvals + Wuzhou-government-sourced construction news) with capacity matching GEM exactly (0.59 bcm/y) and length close (59km reported vs 60km recorded); no duplicate/misclassification found; Operator/Owner/FuelSource attributions and current 'construction' status stand but remain unresolved/unconfirmed for this specific segment pending a later recheck.
